problem: Interpreting Indian tax law is hard because of frequent legislative amendments, complex statutory structures, and the need for precise citation.
method: TaxFlow: a domain-specific legal assistant combining hybrid (dense + sparse, FAISS-based) Retrieval-Augmented Generation with LLaMA-3 over a curated corpus of Indian tax statutes, government gazettes and case law. It applies structured extraction, segmentation, dense-sparse indexing, temporal validity filtering so retrieved provisions reflect the legally effective version at query time, and critique-driven generation.
key_assumptions: The legally effective version of a provision at query time can be determined and filtered programmatically
A curated Indian tax corpus and gazettes capture the relevant amendment history
main_contribution: An end-to-end hybrid RAG legal assistant with temporal validity filtering, reporting 96.5% accuracy and 95.0% F1 on a unified Indian tax law benchmark.
datasets: Curated Indian tax statutes, government gazettes, and case law
Unified Indian tax law benchmark (composition not stated in abstract)
baselines: Representative baseline systems (not named in the abstract)
results: 96.5% accuracy and 95.0% F1-score, with reported improvements over representative baselines and in BLEU/ROUGE-L linguistic quality.
limitations: Only the abstract was accessible (publisher returned HTTP 403), so baselines, temporal-filtering mechanism and benchmark details cannot be verified
Temporal validity is filtered rather than scored, and no comparison to a soft temporal re-ranker is described
Single-country tax domain; no public benchmark release is stated in the abstract
code_availability: Not stated in abstract; full text was not accessible (HTTP 403).

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: TaxFlow is a system paper that hard-filters to the effective version inside a fixed hybrid-RAG stack; the proposed idea claims retrieval-agnostic soft temporal re-ranking and a new overlapping-revision benchmark, neither of which is described here.
relation_to_idea.basis: Same problem (amended statutes requiring the legally effective version) and the same conceptual component (temporal validity in retrieval), but the mechanism is a hard filter inside an end-to-end system and evaluation is single-domain accuracy/F1. Basis is the abstract only.
